subject.title: fix: record cron delivery failures as warnings

question: Should a successful isolated cron execution with failed final delivery remain `status=ok` plus `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, or should OpenClaw add `warning` as a fourth public cron execution status?
rationale: The current types and public CLI documentation establish a three-state execution contract separate from delivery state, while this PR expands Gateway and plugin-hook contracts and alters scheduler semantics.

options.title: Keep execution and delivery separate
options.body: Retain `ok` for successful execution and present undelivered final replies through delivery-specific diagnostics and UI treatment.

options.title: Sponsor a warning-status contract
options.body: Adopt `warning` only with an explicit public API compatibility plan covering Gateway clients, plugin hooks, CLI/UI semantics, backoff, and documentation.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Close or defer the broader warning implementation while the focused execution-versus-delivery fix is resolved on its narrower path.

recommendation.title: Keep execution and delivery separate
recommendation.body: Retain `ok` for successful execution and present undelivered final replies through delivery-specific diagnostics and UI treatment.

likelyOwner.reason: The isolated-cron runner refactor history and explicit discussion mention make this the strongest available routing candidate for the semantic decision.
